judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 2 (rank 1) Indicators under STRAND 4: WRITING, so any developmental claim would be same-rank and requires substantive evidence. B2.4.3.1.3 'Space words appropriately in sentences' sits under Sub-Strand 3: Writing Letters – Small and Capital and Content Standard B2.4.3.1 on using letter skills to write legibly and boldly, with LC tags 'sentences, spacing, words, writing' — i.e. handwriting/transcription legibility. Neither statement extends, deepens, or increases the complexity of the other; they are parallel same-grade sub-strand skills, and the nomination signals (shared Grade/Strand ancestors, rank gap 0 marked 'weak', weak shared code segments 'b2'/'4', low token and trigram overlap driven by the word 'sentences') are hierarchy, proximity, and wording signals that cannot establish development on their own. There is, however, meaningful pair-specific instructional coherence beyond generic repetition: both are sentence-level written-production skills in the same BASIC 2 Writing strand, and appropriate word spacing reinforces the legibility of the sentences learners write or copy from substitution tables, while sentence-writing practice gives an authentic context for spacing. That is complementary reinforcement without dependency, so symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the supported judgment.
